record.paper_title: Open Problems in Hydrodynamical Approach to Relativistic Heavy Ion Collisions
record.original_question: Which observables can serve as signals of genuine hydrodynamic behavior in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, beyond successful fits by hydrodynamical models, and how can candidates such as shock-wave propagation be identified in order to reduce the remaining conceptual and quantitative uncertainties?

evidence.quote: However, from the quantitative point of view, the present hydrodynamical approach still contains many uncertainties and also some conceptual problems.

Other questions as early thermalization, finite size effects, fluctuations in initial conditions, etc. should also be studied more in detail When these questions are clarified, we will have much more detailed knowledge about the dynamics and properties of the new states of strongly interacting matter.
It is also quite important to look for signals of genuine hydrodynamics, such as shock wave propagation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the hydrodynamical description of relativistic heavy-ion collisions, the system created shortly after impact is modeled as a strongly interacting fluid governed by the local conservation laws ∂_μ T^{μν} = 0 (and ∂_μ j^μ_B = 0 for conserved charges), closed by an equation of state p = p(ε, n_B) and supplemented by initial conditions, a freeze-out prescription, and possibly transport coefficients (shear viscosity η, bulk viscosity ζ). Many measured observables in such collisions — single-particle transverse momentum spectra, elliptic flow v_2 and higher harmonics v_n, HBT radii, etc. — can be fit by hydrodynamical models, but successful fitting alone does not establish that the matter truly behaves as a hydrodynamic fluid, since other (e.g. transport or parton-cascade) descriptions can also reproduce many of these features.

Problem: Identify a set of experimentally measurable observables in relativistic heavy-ion collisions whose presence (or quantitative behavior) would constitute a direct signal of genuine hydrodynamic evolution of the produced matter, as opposed to mere agreement of fits with hydrodynamical models. In particular:

(a) Formulate precise criteria, derivable from the relativistic hydrodynamic equations, that distinguish genuine fluid behavior from non-hydrodynamic dynamics.

(b) Determine whether shock-wave propagation excited by a fast parton traversing the medium — for example, the conical "Mach-cone" structure characterized by a Mach angle cos θ_M = c_s/v, where c_s is the medium speed of sound and v is the source velocity — can be unambiguously identified in two- and three-particle azimuthal correlations triggered by high-p_T particles, and specify under what experimental and theoretical conditions such an identification is robust against backgrounds (deflected jets, Cherenkov gluon radiation, medium-induced bremsstrahlung).

(c) Propose additional candidate signatures (e.g., sound-mode propagation imprinted on flow harmonics, response to localized initial-state perturbations, ridge-like structures, characteristic dependence of v_n on c_s and viscosity) and quantify how they reduce the conceptual and quantitative uncertainties of the hydrodynamic picture.
artifact.status_search_result: The identification of unambiguous signals of genuine hydrodynamic behavior in heavy-ion collisions — and in particular the experimental observation of a Mach-cone shock wave — remains an active and unresolved research problem. Subsequent literature has shown that the originally-claimed Mach-cone signal in three-particle correlations is strongly model-dependent and can be mimicked by deflected jets and other mechanisms, while shock-wave studies in viscous and anisotropic relativistic hydrodynamics continue to appear. No consensus signature has been established.

status_evidence.title: The Mach cone signal and energy deposition scenarios in linearized hydrodynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Magnitude and shape of the shock-wave signal show strong dependence on assumptions about parton evolution and medium interaction.
status_evidence.claim: The shock-wave/Mach-cone signal in heavy-ion collisions is model-dependent and not unambiguously identified.

status_evidence.title: Shock Waves in Relativistic Anisotropic Hydrodynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Shock wave solutions in anisotropic relativistic hydrodynamics are being analyzed.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical analyses of relativistic hydrodynamic shock waves remain an ongoing research topic well after 2006.

status_evidence.title: Head shock vs Mach cone: azimuthal correlations from 2 to 3 parton processes
status_evidence.snippet: Compares head-shock and Mach-cone explanations for azimuthal correlations.
status_evidence.claim: Alternative mechanisms compete with Mach-cone interpretations, indicating the signal of genuine hydrodynamics is still debated.
